citation: WaterModels.jl repository, Los Alamos National Laboratory (github.com/lanl-ansi/WaterModels.jl)
description: WaterModels.jl is a Julia and JuMP package for steady-state optimisation of water distribution networks. It is built as a common platform for evaluating historical and emerging water network formulations and algorithms, and separates problem specifications from mathematical formulations so that the two can be combined freely. The core problems are water flow (feasible flows and heads, single or multiple time periods), optimal water flow (minimum operating cost, for example pump scheduling) and network design (minimum design cost); the core formulations range from nonconvex nonlinear and direction-based models to convex, linear and piecewise-linear relaxations and a linear approximation. It is developed at Los Alamos National Laboratory with support from the U.S. Department of Energy's Advanced Grid Modeling Program under a project on coordinated planning and operation of water and power infrastructures for resilience and reliability. It is site-independent and reads standard network descriptions. The code is on GitHub under a BSD three-clause licence held by Triad National Security, free of charge; the latest tag on 26 September 2026 is v0.9.3. Caveats: the README warns that documentation beyond the quick start guide is under development and may be inaccurate, and it needs mathematical-programming solvers. Simulation uses: network design and operational optimisation, capacity planning, and water-power co-optimisation for resilience. It complements the simulators EPANET (model-epanet) and WNTR (model-wntr).
